Text.name: guidelines
Text.value: Read the question and answer, then determine if it contains a metaphor:

View.style: margin-left: 1em; margin-top: 1em; padding: 0.5em; background: #f8f9fa; border-left: 3px solid #6c757d;

Text.name: metaphor_def_header
Text.value: 📖 DEFINITION:

Text.name: metaphor_def1
Text.value: A METAPHOR is ACTIVE/LIVE figurative language in which a concept is framed, evaluated, or described using another domain in a NON-LITERAL way.

Text.name: metaphor_def2
Text.value: Metaphors must be NOVEL (fresh, invented, not conventional).

Text.name: metaphor_def3
Text.value: Metaphors may appear WITH or WITHOUT explicit comparison words such as 'like' or 'similar to'.

Text.name: core_test_header
Text.value: 🔍 CORE METAPHOR TEST:

Text.name: core_test
Text.value: Ask: Does the passage introduce novel, expressive, or unexpected conceptual framing beyond literal or textbook description?

Text.name: core_test_yes
Text.value: • If YES → metaphor present

Text.name: core_test_no
Text.value: • If NO → not a metaphor

Text.name: personification_header
Text.value: 👤 PERSONIFICATION TEST (KEY RULE):

Text.name: personification_q
Text.value: For personification, ask: Is the attributed action, intention, or behavior vivid, surprising, playful, or clearly invented?

Text.name: personification_yes
Text.value: • YES → metaphor

Text.name: personification_no
Text.value: • NO, sounds normal in news, textbooks, or everyday speech → NOT metaphor

Text.name: analogy_header
Text.value: ⚠️ METAPHORICAL ANALOGIES (IMPORTANT):

Text.name: analogy_rule1
Text.value: The presence of explicit comparison language ('like', 'similar to', 'think of X as Y', etc.) does NOT exclude a metaphor.

Text.name: analogy_rule2
Text.value: An analogy IS ALSO a metaphor if it introduces novel, expressive, or imaginative figurative framing beyond neutral explanation.

Text.name: analogy_example
Text.value: Example: 'Debugging this system is like performing surgery with oven mitts.'

Text.name: metaphor_clear_header
Text.value: ✓ CLEAR METAPHORS — Examples:

Text.name: metaphor_ex1
Text.value: • 'rogue proteins throwing a tantrum inside your cells'

Text.name: metaphor_ex2
Text.value: • 'Your DNA is a recipe book written in a 4-letter alphabet'

Text.name: metaphor_ex3
Text.value: • 'electrons waltzing around the nucleus'

Text.name: metaphor_ex4
Text.value: • 'molecules whispering secrets'

Text.name: metaphor_ex5
Text.value: • 'antibodies going to war'

Text.name: metaphor_ex6
Text.value: • 'a tsunami of medication swept through'

Text.name: metaphor_ex7
Text.value: • 'The star is a cosmic pressure cooker slowly boiling itself'

Text.name: metaphor_not_header
Text.value: ✗ NOT METAPHORS

Text.name: metaphor_not_intro
Text.value: Exclude all of the following:

Text.name: metaphor_not1
Text.value: • DEAD or CONVENTIONAL METAPHORS / TECHNICAL TERMS: 'the cell is a factory', 'DNA is a blueprint', 'genetic code'

Text.name: metaphor_not2
Text.value: • STANDARD PERSONIFICATION: 'the market fears', 'the algorithm decides', 'evolution favors'

Text.name: metaphor_not3
Text.value: • IDIOMS: 'tip of the iceberg', 'here be dragons', 'play mind tricks'

Text.name: metaphor_not4
Text.value: • METONYMY: 'Science says', 'The USA wants'

Text.name: metaphor_not5
Text.value: • SHAPE OR LITERAL RESEMBLANCE: 'mushroom cloud', 'potato-shaped asteroid'

Text.name: metaphor_not6
Text.value: • PURELY LITERAL STATEMENTS: 'The heart pumps blood'

Header.value: Does the answer contain a metaphor?
